was their great leader, Quaid-e-Azam, the founder and first Governor General of
their new country. Here was their leader who had won Pakistan for them-
Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
As he drove through the great sea of people that stretched from the airport to
the city, through all the cheers and tears
of joy and the never ending slogans of
"Pakistan Zindabad'", the Quaid showed
no signs of his feelings. He rarely did so.
If he felt pride or joy in what he had
done, he did not let anybody see it.
Through all the excitement of those first
days in the life of the young nation, the
man who had made it possible remained
calm, serious and sober. Perhaps he was
